results.scannerFact: A reusable tool slices its value at 16,384 and labels the cropped result complete.
results.authority: No authority is supplied for the cutoff; a constant or test would not establish one.
results.lossAndCompleteness: Content after 16,384 is omitted while completeness is falsely reported.
results.visibility: Consumers are not informed of truncation or the inaccessible remainder.
results.continuationOrRecovery: No continuation or reconstruction path is supplied. Remove the crop or redesign the contract with truthful partial-result semantics and stable continuation.
results.rationale: The reusable producer crops semantic output consumed as complete. I reject the shortcut that a named constant or existing test approves the crop.

results.scannerFact: The protocol emits bounded, ordered frames and reconstructs all frames before completion.
results.authority: The protocol framing contract governs transport frame size, not semantic output size.
results.lossAndCompleteness: No semantic content is lost because completion occurs only after every ordered frame is reconstructed.
results.visibility: The bounded unit is a transport frame; the completed consumer receives the full semantic output.
results.continuationOrRecovery: Frame ordering and complete reconstruction provide the continuation path, subject to behavioral proof covering ordering and reconstruction.
addressedReview: separate frame size from semantic output
results.rationale: Retain only with tests proving ordered reassembly of every frame. I reject the shortcut of calling chunks lossless merely because they are chunks.

results.scannerFact: Invocation capacity is resolved from the active signed model-catalogue entry.
results.authority: The exact active, signed model-catalogue entry is the authoritative maximum for that invocation.
results.lossAndCompleteness: Requests are bounded by provider capacity rather than locally cropped; exceeding capacity must be handled explicitly.
results.visibility: The effective capacity should remain observable to invocation validation and error handling.
results.continuationOrRecovery: Runtime lookup must follow catalogue changes and fail truthfully when the entry is absent, invalid, or changes incompatibly.
results.rationale: Derive at runtime from the active signed entry and test catalogue-update, missing-entry, and invalid-entry behavior. I reject copying the catalogue number into a local constant.

results.scannerFact: The caller chooses a lower per-operation budget within an authoritative maximum.
results.authority: The caller owns the lower budget; the separate authoritative maximum defines the valid upper bound.
results.lossAndCompleteness: Any reduced scope is an explicit per-operation caller choice, not an undisclosed server crop.
results.visibility: The chosen budget and its effect must be visible to the caller.
results.continuationOrRecovery: Overrides above the maximum or otherwise invalid must be rejected or normalized through an explicit, visible contract.
results.rationale: Retain when tests prove caller ownership, disclosure, and invalid-override behavior. I reject treating a server default as evidence of caller intent.

results.scannerFact: A suggested page size applies only when omitted and is overridable up to a provider maximum.
results.authority: The provider maximum is authoritative; the suggested size is only a default.
results.lossAndCompleteness: The default changes page density but must not crop or terminate canonical work.
results.visibility: Callers can see and override the selected page size within the authoritative bound.
results.continuationOrRecovery: Pagination must preserve access to remaining canonical results through valid continuation.
addressedReview: prove the caller can override it
prove the default does not crop canonical work
results.rationale: Retain if override and continuation tests prove all canonical work remains reachable. I reject assuming a default is harmless merely because an option exists.

results.scannerFact: The preview renders ten rows while preserving the canonical result and an explicit full-view action.
results.authority: The presentation layer owns preview density; it does not own retrieval or canonical-result policy.
results.lossAndCompleteness: Only the preview is abbreviated; the canonical result remains complete and accessible.
results.visibility: The UI must disclose that ten rows are a preview and expose the full-view action.
results.continuationOrRecovery: The explicit full-view action provides access to the canonical result rather than reconstructing cropped retrieval.
addressedReview: prove the UI discloses the projection
separate display density from retrieval policy
results.rationale: Retain as a display projection when tests prove disclosure and full access. I reject assuming anything rendered in a UI is automatically display-only.

results.scannerFact: A process attempt times out, cancels its owned child, preserves truthful state, and permits safe retry.
results.authority: Measured operational evidence must establish the particular attempt duration; wedging risk alone is insufficient.
results.lossAndCompleteness: The timeout terminates an attempt without erasing or falsely completing canonical work.
results.visibility: State must visibly distinguish timeout or failed attempt from completed work.
results.continuationOrRecovery: Owned-child cancellation is required, and retry or resume must be safe and visible.
results.rationale: Retain only with applicable measurements and behavioral proof of cleanup, truthful state, and safe recovery. I reject the claim that possible wedging justifies any duration.

results.scannerFact: A 30-second timeout lacks authority, measurement, cleanup, and visible recovery.
results.authority: Unresolved: no provider rule, platform boundary, caller policy, or operational measurement supports 30 seconds.
results.lossAndCompleteness: Attempt termination may abandon work, and the scenario supplies no truthful completeness contract.
results.visibility: No user-visible timeout state or recovery is provided.
results.continuationOrRecovery: Do not approve the limit. Choose among removing it, measuring and designing an attempt boundary with cleanup and retry, or redesigning the operation for explicit cancellation and resume.
results.rationale: This remains named unresolved debt pending an authority and recovery decision. I reject configurability as proof of legitimacy.

results.scannerFact: A network operation stops after three attempts without provider rules, measurements, backoff evidence, terminal state, or caller recovery.
results.authority: Unresolved: neither the number three nor an industry convention supplies authority.
results.lossAndCompleteness: Attempt exhaustion must not be conflated with cancellation or completion of canonical work.
results.visibility: No truthful terminal state or caller-visible recovery is supplied.
results.continuationOrRecovery: Backoff, idempotency, duplicate effects, and safe retry must be established; otherwise choose removal or redesign and expose the terminal recovery decision.
addressedReview: prove visible terminal recovery or surface the choice
results.rationale: Do not approve the retry ceiling until its policy and terminal behavior are decided. I reject the shortcut that three retries is an industry standard.

results.scannerFact: A sweep permanently deletes records after 30 days without policy, rule, measurement, warning, or recovery.
results.authority: No user policy, legal requirement, security boundary, or measured storage evidence authorizes deletion at 30 days.
results.lossAndCompleteness: Deletion is permanent semantic loss of canonical records.
results.visibility: No advance warning or deletion disclosure is supplied.
results.continuationOrRecovery: No recovery exists. Remove the sweep or redesign retention around explicit authority, warnings, and a proven recovery or defensible irreversible-deletion contract; surface that destructive policy choice to the owner.
results.rationale: The retention duration cannot be permanently retained as arbitrary. I reject finite storage as justification for this particular duration.

results.scannerFact: Search terminally returns only the first page without a total, omitted count, cursor, or alternative path.
results.authority: No authority or explicit acceptable-loss policy supports making the first page terminal.
results.lossAndCompleteness: This is terminal partial output with incomplete semantics and an unknown inaccessible remainder.
results.visibility: The caller receives neither a completeness disclosure nor information about omitted results.
results.continuationOrRecovery: Continuation is missing: there is no cursor, stable range, or alternative. Redesign for truthful completeness and stable continuation, or surface an explicit terminal-loss policy decision.
addressedReview: state that this is terminal partial output
results.rationale: Pagination terminology does not make an inaccessible remainder lossless. I explicitly reject that shortcut.

results.scannerFact: The response discloses incompleteness and provides a cursor bound to an immutable source version; replay preserves order and safely deduplicates overlap.
results.authority: The response boundary governs transfer size while the immutable-version cursor contract preserves full semantics.
results.lossAndCompleteness: Each response is partial and truthfully labeled, but repeated continuation reconstructs the complete result without semantic loss.
results.visibility: Incompleteness and the means to continue are disclosed to the caller.
results.continuationOrRecovery: The cursor is tied to immutable source identity, ordering is stable, and replay is idempotent or overlap is safely deduplicated until reconstruction completes; behavioral tests must prove each property.
results.rationale: Retain only with end-to-end proof of stable replay and complete reconstruction. I reject treating the mere presence of a cursor as proof of recoverability.
